notes.21: * reproduces the edition’s mark for a sign in the papyrus. Letters the scribe deleted in lines 27 and 28 are not translated. ἰᾶσαι may be an infinitive (“to heal”) or an imperative (“heal the sufferer”). *akinos* is a herb, not securely identified.

nodes.text: of the Father and of the H[o]ly [Spirit and]
* Angels of the L(ord) went up to the m[idst of]
The L(ord) says to them, “Why have you come
up, pure, all-pure ones?” “To receive healing
we have come up, Iao Sabaoth, because you
For strangury, to heal the sufferer:
